question: Measure marketing that parents pay for affiliated-commercial nationals (Fidelity, Schwab, Vanguard, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, BofA, Raymond James): read the related-party and services-agreement notes of FY2022-2025 audited statements and Schedule O/Schedule R text for what the administrator fee (line 11a) covers, and whether brand or adviser marketing is borne by the parent or recharged; record per sponsor a filed statement or 'not disclosed'
conclusion_affected: Whether national DAF acquisition cost is near zero (as line 12 shows) or simply carried by parents; the cost-per-new-account comparison of nationals with community foundations in direction-sponsor-marketing-spend.md
rationale: Fidelity reports $0 on line 12 in TY2021-24 but $121-180m a year of line 11a administrator fees; 9 of 13 affiliated-commercial nationals report $0 or blank; Schwab alone reports $20.3m (5.4 bps, about $390 per net new account)

question: For the digital-first sponsors (Daffy, Charityvest, GiveClear/TIFIN Give, Givinga, GoFundMe.org, Goodstack), identify the payee and scope of platform fees and any platform-paid acquisition from public filings only: Schedule L/R related parties, Part VII-B contractors, Schedule O, state charity registrations, and 2021-2026 platform funding announcements; derive a platform-side acquisition-cost range per net new account where a filed or published figure exists
conclusion_affected: Whether digital-first sponsors acquire accounts more cheaply than nationals and CFs or only book the cost off the charity; the digital-first row of the cost-per-account comparison
rationale: Digital-first line 12 is $0.17m pooled TY2021-24 (1.7 bps); Endaoment books 'Sales & marketing' on line 24 ($216k, $265k) and reaches $648 per net new account with it; Charityvest's 'platform fee' ($507k, $653k) names no payee; Givinga's line 11e paid-fundraiser fees are $5.2-18.6m a year
